subject.title: feat: add linux/riscv64 Docker image to multi-platform build

question: Should OpenClaw officially publish riscv64 as a standalone architecture tag first, or include its currently unattested image in the default multi-platform tags?
rationale: This choice establishes an ongoing supported-platform and supply-chain policy; source inspection and contributor proof cannot decide whether the project accepts an attestation exception in default release tags.

options.title: Standalone riscv64 tag first
options.body: Publish versioned riscv64-suffixed tags without changing default manifests until equivalent provenance and release proof are available.

options.title: Include in default manifests
options.body: Accept the documented provenance exception and fold successful riscv64 builds into version, latest, and main tags after existing platform verification.

options.title: Decline official support
options.body: Keep riscv64 images community-maintained rather than adding the architecture to OpenClaw release operations.

recommendation.title: Standalone riscv64 tag first
recommendation.body: Publish versioned riscv64-suffixed tags without changing default manifests until equivalent provenance and release proof are available.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history places Docker release validation and attestation policy work closest to this contributor.
